title: Sidney Bechet's style and reception
summary: Bechet played only solos and was later forgotten.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Sidney Bechet: the man, the horn, the legend

blocks.x: Yeah. Tell me, I've noticed -- I've heard one or two recordings of Bechet, in Miami I heard a few times live, I heard him in Paris when he was an old man. But his -- sometimes I've noticed that his soprano sax style, when he was playing with -- particularly when he was playing Creole numbers, it was surprisingly like some of that (unintelligible) sax.

Well, now, since you mentioned that -- I'm glad you mentioned that, because he had a distinctive way of playing. Nobody played like -- to me, the way we played. And they used him in the band just for solo. He didn't play no parts with the rest of the saxophones.

Oh, no, no, no. He was in there just waiting for the soprano solo. And he had a peculiar way of playing, but they explained to me, that was his only style. That was the way musicians used to play. They got another guy in there -- most of them were playing clarinet, but they had
and this and that. For years and years, he was a forgotten man.
So you think a lot of it was because --
Maybe so, maybe so, I couldn't relate to things, I don't know (unintelligible) and my English was so limited.

I couldn't talk to all the people to find out, but deep in my mind, I knew it was something related, the little that I spoke, I figured I'd draw my own conclusion After the time passed, I come to the conclusion it was something like that, completely different (unintelligible) come from Paris, the same thing, they got -- took me and loved me and my way of playing and everything that I did to him was beautiful and he'd always smile to me, like he liked everything that I done, something like that.
